answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate behavior is proven. Like a sparrow that cannot be in two places at once, one agent cannot wander across many fake accounts without splitting its stake, so creating thousands of identities becomes expensive rather than free. A bridge between reputation and stake lets honest agents build trust over verified work, while attackers lose funds with every detected duplicate, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
